clue.text: The French girls cover miles in Western territories

parts.note: la is the French feminine word for 'the'

indicators.note: the two girls together wrap around, or cover, the miles abbreviation

parts.note: Tina and Erica are two girls' names

explanation.surface: French women expand their range across the lands of the West.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The French' is not a link phrase but supplies the French article; 'girls' gives two names, wrapped round the miles abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Latin America lies in the Western hemisphere, a collection of countries and territories there.

clue.text: Scholarly composer acted as conductor outside

indicators.note: the verb for conducting sits around, outside, the composer's name

parts.note: a conductor leads, so acted as conductor gives led
Thomas Arne was the English composer of Rule, Britannia

explanation.surface: An erudite musician also took the baton.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: someone scholarly is well read and erudite.

clue.text: Farmers undertake it up to their declining years

parts.note: till means until, up to a point in time
old age is often called one's declining years

explanation.surface: Farmers keep working the land right into their old age.
explanation.definitionFit: Tilling the soil, preparing land for crops, is work farmers carry out.

clue.text: It sustains teachers with old poetry books

parts.note: the NUT was the National Union of Teachers in Britain
rime is an archaic spelling of rhyme, verse
NT, the New Testament, is a set of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: Teachers are kept going by classic verse and literature.
explanation.definitionFit: Nourishment is what sustains the body, so the answer is something that sustains.

clue.text: Effectively copes with sports gatherings

definitions.meaning: to meet a demand or challenge is to deal with it successfully
athletics or racing events are called meetings, or in the plural this word

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: to deal satisfactorily with a need, and plural sporting fixtures such as a race meet.

clue.text: Dispute about a popular bishop's illusory hope?

indicators.note: the quarrel word goes around, about, the other letters

parts.note: a row is a quarrel or dispute
in means fashionable or popular
B is the chess notation abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A quarrel over a well-liked bishop, whose hopes may be ill-founded.
explanation.walkthrough: Chasing the end of the rainbow, or its pot of gold, is a proverbial vain hope, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: A rainbow can symbolise a hope that is elusive, like the gold at its end that is never found.

clue.text: Copper upset rower about bill for liqueur

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

indicators.note: the turned rower goes around, about, the bill
in a down clue, upset means the word is turned upside down, read backwards

parts.note: an oar is a rower in rowing slang
AC, account, is a bill

explanation.surface: A policeman knocks over an oarsman over the drinks tab.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'upset' reads the rower upwards, giving RAO; 'about' then wraps it round the bill.
explanation.definitionFit: Curacao is an orange-flavoured liqueur from the Caribbean island of that name.

clue.text: Given book, revised blurb at home — one has no discretion

indicators.note: a revised text has been rearranged, so the following letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A publisher reworks the jacket copy at home, but someone can't keep a secret.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revised' rearranges the three words after it into LABBERMOUTH, which follows the book abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A blabbermouth is a person who talks indiscreetly and reveals secrets.

clue.text: Part of plant allowed to produce advertising material

parts.note: a leaf is part of a plant
let means permitted or allowed

explanation.surface: A bit of foliage is permitted to become promotional literature.
explanation.definitionFit: A leaflet is a printed sheet handed out to advertise or inform.

clue.text: Bon mot of English soldier reversing into carriage

indicators.note: the turned soldier goes into the carriage

parts.note: a pram is a baby carriage

indicators.note: the soldier is read backwards, reversing

parts.note: a GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: A witty remark from an English soldier backing into a carriage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reversing' turns GI into IG, which goes into PRAM.
explanation.definitionFit: A bon mot is a witty saying, as is an epigram.

clue.text: Paris girl created second ballet, except for opening

parts.note: made means created
a mo is a moment, a second

indicators.note: the first letter of the ballet's name is dropped

parts.note: Giselle is a famous Romantic ballet

explanation.surface: A Parisian girl choreographed a new ballet, apart from its first night.
explanation.walkthrough: 'except for opening' removes G from GISELLE, leaving ISELLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Mademoiselle is the French title for a young unmarried woman, so a girl in Paris.

clue.text: Asian girl entering African state stopped short

indicators.note: the girl goes inside the shortened state
the state's name loses its final letter, cut short

parts.note: Benin is a country in West Africa
gal is an informal word for a girl

explanation.surface: A woman crossing into an African country is halted at the border.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stopped short' trims the African country's last letter, giving BENI; 'entering' then puts the girl inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A Bengali is a person from Bengal, in South Asia.

clue.text: Detectives tailing press employee are rather sour

indicators.note: the detectives follow behind, tailing, the other letters

parts.note: a sub is a subeditor on a newspaper
an are is a metric unit of area, abbreviated A
CID is the Criminal Investigation Department of British police

explanation.surface: Police following a journalist are in a bad mood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'are' looks like a verb, but it is the unit of area, A.
explanation.definitionFit: Subacid means slightly acid, moderately sour in taste.

clue.text: Clothe bear right away

indicators.note: the right letter is taken away

parts.note: to bear something is to endure it

explanation.surface: Dress a bear quickly, straight away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'right away' looks like 'immediately'; it means remove R.
explanation.definitionFit: Endue is a literary verb meaning to clothe or invest someone.

clue.text: Space to manoeuvre something lifted in pub

definitions.meaning: drinkers lift the elbow in a pub, so jokingly the room they need to do it

explanation.definitionFit: Elbow room means enough space to move; 'lifting the elbow' is slang for drinking.

clue.text: Graduate entertains slimmer's objective, eating off this?

indicators.note: the graduate holds, entertains, the other letters

parts.note: a BA is a Bachelor of Arts, a graduate
a dieter hopes to lose a double chin and have only one

explanation.surface: A graduate on a diet wonders whether to eat off fine plates.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is cryptic: a plate of fine porcelain is something to eat off.
explanation.definitionFit: Bone china is a fine porcelain used for plates and other tableware.

clue.text: Shabby Shakespearean character going to sound school

parts.note: Moth is a fairy in A Midsummer Night's Dream

indicators.note: the school's name is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: Eton is the famous English public school

explanation.surface: A character from Shakespeare goes off to a good school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sound' looks like an adjective meaning reliable; it signals a homophone.
explanation.definitionFit: Something moth-eaten is worn and tatty, so shabby.

clue.text: Ill-fated vessel like Oceanus

definitions.meaning: the liner that sank on its maiden voyage in 1912
Oceanus was one of the Titans of Greek myth

explanation.definitionFit: The doomed liner bore this name, and the adjective means pertaining to the Titans.

clue.text: Reportedly the speaker hollers, making us stare

indicators.note: the phrase is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: the speaker is I, and to holler is to bawl

explanation.surface: The man at the microphone shouts so loudly that we gape.
explanation.definitionFit: To eyeball someone is to stare at them hard.

clue.text: A carnivore? Caught one eating grass

indicators.note: the outer letters take in, eat, the grass

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
I is the Roman numeral for one
oat is a cereal grass

explanation.surface: Is it a meat-eater when spotted munching grass?
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark is fair: the coati, a raccoon relative, is in the order Carnivora though it eats much else.
explanation.definitionFit: The coati is a South American mammal of the raccoon family, an animal in the carnivore order.

clue.text: Fuel container extremely serviceable during summit

indicators.note: the extreme letters come during, inside, the summit

parts.note: a crest is the top or summit of a hill

indicators.note: the first and last letters, the extremes, of the word are taken

explanation.surface: A fuel tank stays useful right through to the top.
explanation.definitionFit: A cresset is a metal basket holding burning fuel as a beacon or torch.

clue.text: Crash into motorists, initially inspiring colourful language

indicators.note: the crash word goes into the motorists

parts.note: the AA is the Automobile Association, a British motoring organisation
to ram is to crash into

indicators.note: the first letters of the next two words are taken

explanation.surface: Crashing into drivers provokes some colourful swearing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'colourful language' looks like the definition; only 'language' is, as 'colourful' gives C.
explanation.definitionFit: Aramaic is an ancient Semitic language, spoken in Jesus's time.

clue.text: Tendency to rise, put out by Republican aim

indicators.note: out signals the word put is knocked out of shape

parts.note: an end is an aim or goal

explanation.surface: A rising trend is spoiled by Republican goals.
explanation.definitionFit: An uptrend is an upward trend, a tendency for prices or figures to climb.

clue.text: Line up formal attire

definitions.meaning: evening wear, as in formal clothing

explanation.definitionFit: To dress troops is to align them in rank; the noun also means clothing or formal wear.

clue.text: People removing marks inside container with notched edge

indicators.note: what remains goes inside the container

parts.note: a crate is a container

indicators.note: the marks letter is taken out of the people word

parts.note: men means people
M was the abbreviation for the German mark

explanation.surface: Men taking off the labels inside a box with a jagged edge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'removing' leaves EN, as the German mark is an old currency abbreviated M; 'inside' sets that in the container.
explanation.definitionFit: Crenate is a botanical term for leaves with a scalloped or notched edge.

clue.text: In Aachen, ban engineering plant producing poison

indicators.note: the plant sits within the run of words that follow

explanation.surface: A German city bans technical work on a toxic plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Henbane is a poisonous plant of the nightshade family.

clue.text: Way to enter collectively, given place in office

indicators.note: the way goes into the collective phrase

parts.note: in all means altogether, collectively
St is the abbreviation for street, a way

explanation.surface: A path for everyone to walk in, given a post in office.
explanation.definitionFit: To install someone is to put them formally into an office or post.

clue.text: Cleric in northern town, one with a reduced staff

parts.note: Eccles is a town near Manchester in northern England
I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: the staff word loses its final letter

parts.note: a stick is a staff

explanation.surface: A churchman from a northern town walks with a short cane.
explanation.definitionFit: An ecclesiastic is a clergyman, a cleric.
